newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin holds Kremlin talks with Spanish king.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin holds Kremlin talks with Spanish king.

text.p: Spain's King Juan Carlos met Russian President Boris Yeltsin in the Kremlin on Tuesday for talks touching on bilateral economic ties and the vexed issue of NATO's eastward expansion.
"We have many important problems to discuss," Yeltsin told reporters before ushering his royal guest into private talks.

The king is on a three-day state visit, his second to Moscow. He was due to meet Patriarch Alexiy, head of the Russian Orthodox Church, later on Tuesday. A formal banquet will be held in the Kremlin in the king's honour on Tuesday evening.
Juan Carlos will also open an exhibition of Spanish art at Moscow's Pushkin Museum, to include paintings by Pablo Picasso, Joan Miro and Salvador Dali.

Russian media have given the royal visit prominent coverage, drawing parallels between Spain's transition to democracy since the 1970s under Juan Carlos's supervision and their own country's passage from communism to a free society.
The liberal daily Sevodnya said Juan Carlos had much to teach his Russian hosts in the art of uniting and reconciling a divided nation.
Russia and Spain signed a Treaty of Friendship and Cooperation in 1994 but are keen to increase trade, which Itar-Tass news agency said rose almost 50 percent last year to total $1.87 billion.

Moscow's main export is oil and oil products, while Spain exports foodstuffs to Russia. Tass said trade ministry officials predict an increase in Spanish exports of meat, edible oils, fruit and vegetables this year.
